rgN4iu8T2w0.description:
Matt has gone for his first trip back to Texas.  I am on my own doing everything for all 7 of my kids and pets while still trying to fit in the things I normally do (workout, recovery massage a few times a month, my real work...not house work, etc).  It may seem like an easy thing to do this, but when the care of the house and family are usually split between two people, it's quite a task to take on alone.  There's taking out the trash...checking mail...feeding dogs....gas in the cars.......cooking meals....making the next day lunches...soccer runs......grocery shopping.....general house cleaning....dishes...laundry....slashing boxes so they fit in the trash cans....homework help...school pickups and drop offs...cleaning up dog messes....music practice and lessons....changing bed sheets....the list goes on and on.  There's a lot we do around here and not having Matt home makes a big impact on our family.  We know he needs to be in Texas right now, though, so please send your positive and peaceful thoughts to him.

We had the amazing opportunity to attend the world premiere of The Rise of SuperMouth at the Dances With Films Festival in Hollywood, CA. It was a great movie--and I have to tell you, it truly inspired us to brush our teeth! In the movie, the SuperMouth Squad, a team of superhero dentists, tries to stop the villainous candymaker, Cavitar, from spreading Sugar Bugs to ruin all the teeth throughout the galaxy. It was so funny and so well done! When we got home all Owen begged to use his new SuperMouth mouthbrushes and mouthpaste to brush away all the Sugar Bugs from the day. My jaw hit the ground since he is one who usually won't even use toothpaste!  As a mom, I am so excited about this toothpaste because it has probiotics in it! The movie was excellent, the superheros were so funny, and on top of it, having these mouthcare products that are custom for each of my kids is amazing! Owen is enjoying brushing his teeth and that's for sure a win! We want to thank SuperMouth for making our attendance at the festival possible and brushing our teeth SUPER fun! Check out all the oral care products seen in the movie at supermouth.com. Thanks for watching & don't forget to give us a THUMBS UP!

We have lost someone very very special in our lives.  Ironically, everyone that knows our beloved music teacher feels exactly how we do--and that speaks volumes for who she is as a person. We have had way too many funerals this year.  For me personally, I have not attended more than 1 or 2 funerals for my entire life. This has been a very hard year. Although this was not a "fun" trip to go on, since we would much rather have our beloved voice teacher and dear friend here on the Earth with us, we were able to see old friends and the reunion with them was nice, so there were some nice parts of this trip.  I caught up with a lot of my high school friends as well as getting together with my best friend and her kids.  Please pray for the family of our friend...they are really struggling right now.

It's Day 2 at the beautiful Bass Lake and Pines Resort, and we start our day by doing the most dangerous thing we have ever done on vacation!  I never thought I would be giving my 9 year old a very sharp axe to throw at will....but I did!  After we survived axe throwing, we had seriously the best meal we have had in a VERY long time.  The service was great, and food was absolutely superb (I am picky about food places and I thought my food was not only presented well but tasted great!)  They also brew their own root beer at South Gate Brewing Co. and it was perfection in a glass!  This vacation was far too short and we really want to go back!  Comment if you think we should go back again.....maybe in the snow??

Plan a visit to The Pines Resort!  Your family will have a wonderful time!

Despite how good she might look, she is not a full term baby and she is going to take a while to get to the place other full term babies are.  This is a road I have never been down before and I honestly had no clue how important it truly was to stay pregnant as long as possible.  Obviously babies sometimes come early, or have to come early due to an emergency (such as in our case), but in the past I have often secretly hoped to go into labor early simply because my pregnancy was so uncomfortable at the end....I now know and fully understand how each and every day your baby is inside is a blessing!

My decorations were absolutely perfect and unlike anything I have ever had at a party in my life--honestly prettier than my wedding!!  I'm so thankful for family and friends who came and for family and friends who helped with my very special day.  My sister in law is an AMAZING bow tier (I probably said that in a weird way, but she is!) and she tied all the bows you'll see around the shower.  My mom and sisters made the cupcakes and cookies, my amazing editor Courtney filmed this for me, everyone came together and it was just perfect!!  I also want to thank everyone who came for being covid tested prior to the shower.  I was truly worried people wouldn't come because of that, but everyone still came!  Thank you all for the wonderful gifts for our baby girl---everything is gorgeous and SO helpful since we are starting from scratch with this beautiful baby girl of ours!!!
I also want to thank people who travelled quite far in order to set up decorations and food at my house!!  I know it took one person over 2 hours, but we REALLY appreciate your amazing decorating talents.  We also appreciate overnight shipping to get some of the decorations to our house that we put up ourselves.  So many people really came together on this and I want to thank you all from the bottom of my heart!

iSRL-SvM4PQ.description:
What a SHOCKING turn of events for us!  We decided to head up to New Jersey to visit Diggerland.  We have been once before when Michael was about 2 year old, and Owen is far more obsessed with tractors and diggers that Michael ever was, so we were really excited to go.  Here's the awesome part--they kept the park closed and only let us in for the entire day!!!  So cool right??!!  Here's the crazy part: the weather was insane.  It went from nice, sunny weather to 40 degrees with light rain and wind.  Being from California, we were NOT prepared for such cold weather.  We also didn't have any warm clothes with us.....so we found a few things at Ross (I should have taken the weather more seriously and gotten more) and had a great day!  I just wish I had worn more than a light wind breaker and thin leggings for myself.  My hands got so cold that my fingers were turning white and losing circulation, so you'll notice Matt filmed almost the entire first day at Diggerland for us (thumbs up for that!).  Day 2 was back to normal nice weather--insane!!  Anyway, we made some awesome memories there as a family and if you get the chance, be sure to pay them a visit!!!  (Also the water park is literally one of the cutest I have ever seen, don't you love it?!) Thank you Diggerland for hosting us!!

VERVM6Ti7Es.description:
Today was another VERY full day!  We started off on a super fun mountain coaster and like usual, Owen was scared, but in a surprising turn of events, he realized mountain coasters could be fun and he ended up loving it!  After our stop at Rocky Top Mountain Coaster, we went to Gatlinburg and stopped at Anakeesta.  This is a place you'd hardly know was there because to get there, you drive in a fairly busy downtown area, but you jump on a ski lift and go to the top of the most peaceful mountain full of stuff to do!  It's an amazing hidden gem in my opinion.  Now that we know about it, I can't wait to go back.  Matt, Alyssa, David, Zac and Chris did a super cool tree canopy zip line course while Owen, Michael and I spent time in a refreshing water fountain area.  Afterwards, we all went on this climbing adventure course.  What I loved about it was that anyone young or old could do this course, and that's not always the case for these types of things.  It was gorgeous and peaceful there.  We even had a bear walk up right to where we were about to zipline and someone had to scare it away, which was crazy!  On our way down the ski lift, we saw more bears but this part was probably even cooler because the ski lift happened to stop with us RIGHT ABOVE this huge bear that was climbing a tree!  I mentioned how badly I wanted to see a bear climb a tree, and it literally happened before my eyes.  It was truly magical!  After this it was getting dark, but we still wanted to do one more mountain coaster, so we stopped at Rowdy Bear Mountain Adventure Park and rode the coasters in the dark which was SO COOL!!!  The tracks were all lit up and it looked so cool.  Today was a super fun, super special day for us.  I have so many good memories of this day we spent in Tennessee during our road trip.  Hope you enjoy the vlog!

You guys won't believe this day!  I'm serious--it felt like we were living some kind of dream!  It started off with a stop at Sweet--this amazing candy store. CB1p7o44xn8.description:
Today's vlog was a turning point for me.  I don't usually write a lot about the video here, but I just have to today.  In the past, Epcot has never been my "favorite" park. I always favorite one of the other parks, usually Magic Kingdom, for whatever reason.  But this year, we visited Epcot during the Flower and Garden festival and I can't even describe in words how amazing my day was at Epcot.  I love taking pictures of my kids, and the beautiful places to do that never ended.  I have never been to a Disney park for any special event aside from Mickey's Halloween, and seeing the park as I did was something I'll never forget.  There was this one particular spot we sat and I still reference it to my family as "the oasis".  I have decided I want to recreate that "oasis" somewhere in my backyard.  I'm sure I won't be that successful, but I want to recreate the feeling I had while I saw there at Disney World, enjoying the most perfect weather with my sweet family while beautiful greenery was all around me.  Epcot day was an absolute dream, and I think this vlog clearly depicts how wonderful our day was there.  I really hope you all love this vlog as much as I do because it's one that I have been most excited to share!  

I hope you all have been enjoying tagging along on our trip so far.  Special thanks to Walt Disney World for hosting us, we love partnering with you guys!

He had only been on the bottom two branches, but when he saw the huge buffalo coming, he climbed straight to the top!  As I watched the scene play out, I was imagining the tree branches snapping below him, or all kinds of other scenarios.  I didn't film as much because I was more concerned with staying away form the buffalo myself while also remaining close enough that I could tell Chris what to do to stay safe.   I guess I'm glad my kids are strong  and confident climbers!

rxJvQrvh5tg.description:
Wow, what a fun day (for me at least!)  I took a day for myself, let my husband care for the kids.  I spent almost my whole day learning a new sport and getting all the gear I will need so I can continue to play.  I went out with my parents for golf.  They've been taking David but I have never gone.  Since I cannot play basketball due to social distancing guidelines, I figured now was a great time to pick up a sport that does not require contact with other people.  My dad is a semi-professional golfer, so he was more than happy to give me some tips and, as you'll see in the video, with a little persuasion, I even got him to go shopping with me!  I am really excited about this new chapter of starting something I have not done before.  However, when I woke up the next day, muscles I never even knew I had were SO sore!!!  We also opened fan mail in today's video.  We have had a hold on mail since late last year.  First we moved so we put the mail on hold, then when we were ready to receive it in February of this year, our service completely was shut down as businesses began to close.  We finally got special permission to get our mail, 10 months later!  Anyway, thank you all for so patiently waiting for us to get this mail, and thank you for sending such nice things to us!  We always feel so happy when we open our fan mail.  HUGS!!

Somehow David managed to catch one of the giant fish instead of the tiny fish that people usually catch there. It was a fantastic day that finished with a fantastic luau.  Thanks for coming along!

What started as a completely normal day got a bit crazy really fast.  We realized we left one of our kids, which honestly don't happen often since the kids are old enough to jump in the car when we say "lets go", so I guess this is my second public mom fail in the past 2 weeks (see the other big one here: https://youtu.be/b-S-PkI08B4) Then we had to leave our workout abruptly because a certain someone stripped down in public.  After that we got some horrible news about our sweet Kona, who is still back in California.  We will be sure to update you on Kona as we can.  As always, my parenting vlogs aren't a direct "do this" but rather, I hope they come across gently so you can learn from me of things to do and things not to do--like leaving a kid behind lol.  Thanks so much for watching us!  I really do appreciate that you guys watch the videos we make!  HUGS!

Cm7z3y6nmwQ.description:
I've been so excited to finally share with you what we have been up to since moving to Hawaii.  It's something new and different, and it put us completely out of our comfort zone.  I'm so incredibly proud of my kids for being able to perform live like this and make so many people smile.  It brings joy to my heart to see the happiness our music brings to people from around the world. Also in today's vlog, my iPhone 11 that was brand new broke, so I was worried this vlog would be no good. Over 60 files were lost that could not be recovered due to the phone not being able to power back on.  Luckily we had a VERY full day so you actually don't even notice the missing clips.  I also just realized as I was typing this that we went to both Target and Walmart in the same video.  We usually don't go to both, but they were across the island from each other :)
Anyway, I just want to express once more how proud I am of the kids for being able to step out in front of hundreds of strangers and share their talent of music and singing.  Something else I realized during this journey is that I might have a drummer on my hands!  I always said I didn't want any of my kids to play the drums, but look how happy Michael is as he drums on the back of the ukulele.  As always, thank you for watching us and please leave us your thumbs up!

This is probably one of the cutest videos on our entire channel.  I literally LIVE through my kids.  My whole life has meaning because I am a mom, and I thrive on giving my kids experiences that we both will remember.  This day was one of them.  Wait till you see my sweet Owen's reactions to meeting the Disney characters at the Aulani.  It's just so cute, innocent and sweet.  Beyond that, we went to a FANTASTIC luau, we snorkeled at Rainbow Reef (including myself the chicken!  I know it doesn't seem like much but it took me a bit to get in, and it was totally worth it!) We checked out every water slide and pool at the resort, we pin traded, we listened to relaxing Hawaiian music.  We had a fantastic, fun-filled day of Disney awesomeness! We can't wait to visit the Aulani again!  Everything was perfect.

DGh9YSPwhwE.description:
As you guys know, I absolutely LOVE basketball.  I didn't realize I loved this sport until I was 20 years old, but as soon as I first picked up a ball, it was as if I had always played.  Somehow I was able to make all kinds of shots from all angles.  What I didn't know were any of the positions or even what a layup was, so I asked people at the gym to help me.  Then I joined the intramural team at my college where I felt very out of place because everyone else had been playing for years except myself.  The more I played, the more I loved the game.  I became obsessed and was at the gym 5 hours a day shooting hoops.  I knew whoever I married had to be good at basketball.  When I met Matt, that was one of the first things I asked him--Are you good at basketball?  He took me to a professional basketball game for our first date :)
Now fast forward to how it's been at every gym I have ever tried to play a pickup game at....nobody wants the girls to play.  I have gotten used to it, but it doesn't make it right.  Even when I could play better than some of the guys on the court (I was in a lot better shape before having twins), I would still be last picked until people got to know me.  Once the guys knew me, they'd always pick me, but being chosen last or even not at all, even over someone trying to run on a sprained ankle definitely hurt.  I understand that many of you won't care about what I have to say in this video, but since this is my YouTube channel, I'm making videos that are important to me.  This is my life and I want to document it.  I want to show my kids that I was one good at basketball, even though I'm not nearly as good now as I was 10 years ago.  I want my daughter not to be afraid to play a sport she loves, even though being excluded can be pretty discouraging.  Had I stopped trying when I realized that hardly any women play basketball, it would have been quite a shame.  I actually saved someone's life once on a basketball court. 
 I'll have to give that story later.  You just never know where your life might lead, and my basketball journey has done some incredible things for my life.  Thanks for watching my video and kudos to anyone who read all this way down! Love you guys!!

hT-wMbGh5xI.description:
Just a heads up, this vlog might tug on your heartstrings a bit.  We are coming to the end of our road trip, and one of our last stops is the most special.  We not only visit my twin brother and sister, but we visit my grandma who is about to turn 99 years old! This is a touching vlog for me personally, because if you recall last year, she was moved from the home I knew her in and taken to this new place where we visited her.  It really got to me when my kids were singing to her because she was enjoying it so much, and I kept wondering in the back of my mind if they would ever get to do that again. We had a great time with grandma.  We got her new clothes and a new purse.  We took her to a play and out to dessert so she could have an outing outside of the home where she now lives. This vlog may be longer than normal, but when you're spending time with your 99 year old grandma, it's hard to cut things out. Thank you all for being a part of grandma's life.  I tell her every time I'm with her that she is famous.  She always loved telling me of celebrities or important people she had met, and I've always wanted her to know she's just as good as any of them. Anyway, thank you all again for coming along on this journey with us!  I know you can't comment here on YouTUbe, so please, please, please head over to our Instagram and comment!  I really do read all the comments on Instagram (and Facebook/Twitter). Plus, I want to hear what you think of the new boyfriend!  Is there a wedding in our future??!! HUGS you all!

RrpRMnKIwJI.description:
There are only 2 places in the world that you can do what we did in today's video. We rode at top speed down a 1000 foot hill inside a giant 12 foot tall water ball at the Outdoor Gravity Park. The craziest part is that once you get in the ball, you're in.  You can't get out till you've ridden all the way down the hill! The official term is called Zorbing and it is done inside an Ogo ball, and it is simply amazing!  The water inside the ball allows you to roll at top speeds down twisting tracks, and it feels even faster than it looks!  I hope you guys love this video, because it's pretty awesome footage! If you head to Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, be sure to book your Outdoor Gravity Park experience because it's one of the best things to do in Pigeon Forge for sure!! We went to our first NASCAR race in Daytona, Florida and it was absolutely amazing! We saw all kinds of crashes, including a huge 15 car pileup! The race was postponed due to heavy rain and reschedule to the next day when it was SWELTERING hot and humid, but we still got out on the actual race track and got to sign the finish line and meet lots of drivers. YgAO9A8vVO0.description:
If you want to see poisonous snakes, alligators, huge loud bugs, turtles, fish, birds and get caught in the biggest rainstorm flood you can imagine, go to the Florida Everglades!!!!  Talk about a week of adventure, and we're still here to talk about it!  We had giant lizards (the size of a dog) at our hotel, too!  We visited Everglades National Park and went to all of the different visitor centers.  We even did the tram tour at Shark Valley.  We drove the Loop Road.  We did it all, and we saw pretty much every amazing thing you can see.  We saw so many alligators!  Only one of the parks had giant grasshoppers though. There were so many in one of the fields, you couldn't even walk there or you'd be covered and have them bumping in to you as they jumped and flew around. They're called a lubber, and we haven't seen bugs so huge ever! We even got caught in a major hurricane season tropical storm.  You'll see....it was insane!

For this vlog, I am alone with Owen and Michael for a week in Florida while Matt takes the big kids to another state for summer camp. The boys and I had so much fun together.  I braved Orlando and took them on some adventures!  We went to Gatorland where Michael got VERY close to a python and he also got to sit on a real alligator, feed alligators and more! We visited the Kennedy Space Center--WOW!!!  This was seriously so cool!!  I'm honestly not that "into" space stuff, and I was very very interested and quite impressed with everything NASA that they had to share there.  Michael is obsessed with outer space and he was in paradise there! We went to the Orlando Science center where the boys got to have a lot of pretend playtime and hands on science experience. We went window shopping at Disney Springs, I took the boys to Cocoa Beach and a few other little places.  We made so many memories and it really was a super fun week, despite my arms being strained. SpoGXPj-MSQ.description:
Talk about extreme! We went on the longest zip line in Scandinavia--it was extremely fast (90km per hour!), and very very cold!  We saw amazing waterfalls! We rode a train with beautiful views and some of the steepest drop offs in the world! The mountain train is one of the steepest railways in the world, with 80% of the railway being over a 5% grade! We found giant icicles, ate delicious homemade waffles and drank hot chocolate.  Day 2 in Norway was amazing, but wait till you see days 3 and 4--even more fun stuff to come! oVXqCUpwNpI.description:
If your house was on fire, would you be able to grab what you need and go?  What about in an earthquake, hurricane, tornado or other emergency? Two years ago, we decided to have our kids prepare "go bags" that they would keep in their room in case of an emergency.  Ironic as it is, we did not take them with us when we moved to Hawaii, and just a few weeks after moving there, we were hiding in a room because of the missile threat.  It goes to show that you really never do know when you might need to get out as quickly as possible.  Being prepared is a very comforting feeling. In today's video, we decided to give our go bags a major upgrade.  All the kids got their own backpack, Matt and I got a family bag, and we even got some for our aunts and parents (shh, they don't know yet--it's a surprise!) The new bags are from Emergency Zone and they're fully loaded with all of the essentials from water to first aid to things to keep you occupied if you're away from home for a long time. We also updated our food storage by adding a bunch more food with a super long shelf life from Legacy Foods. We added some new things as well--a portable toilet made from a bucket and some go bags for our dogs! The other important part of today's video is that we practiced our evacuation process as a family.  We went over our meeting spot and what to do in different types of emergencies. I think this helps the kids feel confident, if they ever were to have to use these skills. Be sure to tell us in the comments your tips and tricks that your family uses and let us know if you have any questions! We will answer them next week. 
Check out our Go Bags from Emergency Zone: http://www.emergencyzone.com/Default.asp
Check out our Food Storage from Legacy: https://www.legacyfoodstorage.com/

Q1HjSN9JASY.description:
We got a very special experience while living in Hawaii.  We just so happened to visit the Big Island right before the huge eruption of Kilauea! It was crazy because as we were in Volcanoes National Park, we noticed a LOT more action from the places where you can see the lava.  We noticed a lot bigger bubbling and taller spurts of lava where it used to be a lot smaller and harder to see.  We also noticed some fissures we didn't remember from the last few visits to the park...then we left and got word that the volcano had erupted!  It totally explained everything we saw while we were there.  It's cool that we got footage of this beautiful park as it was, but also sad because it's going to look so different next time we go there.  We also had a super yummy refresher at Makanis Magic Pineapple Shak then we had to hurry and leave for the day.  Thanks for spending the day with us! Get a personalized video from us to you! rUG9fivOD68.description:
Chris got bit by a lion - That was the exact text I frantically sent my mom and sister from out of the country, hoping I had the reception to let them know and see what we should do.  We went on a super fun Disney Cruise for Halloween this year.  This was our first Disney cruise and it happened to fall in October when they were doing Halloween on the High Seas.  We had so much fun experiencing Halloween fun at sea!  Everything about the cruise was fantastic although in my opinion, the food was better on Princess and Carnival.  Anyway, back to the lion bite.  So we got on this bus to get into town and the guy on the bus was telling us about this amazing opportunity we could have where you could hold and feed baby lions.  He acted like it was a sanctuary and he said how the baby lions would help hold their bottles of milk like human babies.  It sounded so cute so we bought our tickets for the 45 minute drive out there.  Once we got there, it wasn't at all as the guy described it.  It was a restaurant with 3 small cages that held all kinds of exotic cats.  Once inside the first cage, we found out there was no feeding of baby lions or tigers.  The lion in there was a few months old and very feisty.  The handler was holding the lion for Chris to take a picture as everyone did who went in the cage and as he finished the photo, the lion turned and bit Chris on the shoulder while clawing him on his back and opposite shoulder.  It all happened so fast that I didn't even realize how crazy it was. MY KID WAS BITTEN BY A LION!  In another country!  After leaving the area and gathering my thoughts I started realizing that there could be bacteria in the bite, etc, etc and I started freaking out.  I tried to text my family back in the US but my texts wouldn't go through. I put hand sanitizer all over the area and on his scratches and took him to the medical office on the ship right when we got back.  Anyway, it was an experience we won't forget.  When we got back home we took him to the doctor and she said he was looking good and because it wasn't a super deep bite we were lucky!  She also said this was her first patient of her entire career that came in for a lion bite haha :)  
Anyway, the cruise was fantastic.  The servers were absolutely fantastic and the shows were phnomenal!  Disney has the best entertainment by far!  Hope you enjoy watching our Halloween Cruise Special!

58GtB2iObqs.description:
This holiday season, our family spent the majority of our time working on the biggest charity event we have ever done.  We decided to donate clothes, toys and food to over 1,000 people.  This was a HUGE task, and I began to think I had bitten off more than I could chew, but we pulled it off!  This videos shows the highlights of what we did.  We spent about a week buying all the different items, a few days sorting them, and another week donating them.  My favorite times would be when we would notice a little kid and by the time they walked by us, we had some clothes for them in their exact size.  It is so important to give to others and light the world around you. We all need to be beacons of light in a world that has much darkness in it.  We love every one of the people we served this holiday season and we are thankful for the opportunity we had to give back in such a large way this year.  Remember, it is not our job to judge who is in need.  We do not know the personal situation of anyone we helped, other than finding them doing laundry at a laundromat on Christmas Eve, walking alone, living in their car....or maybe we just had a hunch or saw a mother with a lot of small children, anyone could use a smile because you really do not know their personal situation.  Thanks for watching & don't forget to give us a THUMBS UP! | Subscribe: http://bit.ly/FFPSubscribe

RoblDKRD6Q4.description:
We hardly see snow where we live, so sand sledding sounded like a perfectly fun activity as we were driving and saw a sign for White Sands National Monument.  The funny thing is that we decided to go there because we thought it would be pretty (and we needed a break from driving), but when we got there we saw people carrying snow sleds and discs.  We asked if people were really allowed to sled and they said yes, so we bought some discs (from the National Park Service--they sell them right there and monitor their use!) and had a fantastic time!  This is actually not technically sand, it is gypsum and it is very cold due to a water table beneath the sand that keeps the temperature down.  When we didn't have shoes on, our feet were freezing!  This is definitely a fun stop when you're on a road trip, we recommend it! Thanks for watching!  Don't forget to give us a THUMBS UP!

S7Tf452S5SY.description:
If you go to Jamaica, Dunn's River Falls is a MUST-DO! We almost bypassed this excursion to do something else, and I am SO glad we did this.  It was an amazing, once-in-a-lifetime experience.  It is for adults, no one young is even permitted, but so so much fun! The water was so nice and cool feeling. I am usually the timid one when it comes to water activities, but I felt safe the entire time, and if I was unsure, a guide was there to help out.  The twins and Michael were too small for this activity so they stayed in the kiddie care back on the ship while we did this.  Also, there is a "dry" route you can take if you don't want to go in the water.  It's a paved path that goes alongside the waterfall and has lookouts so you can see your friends and family who are getting wet.

This was one of the coolest places we have ever been.  We visited the Cayman Turtle Farm, an attraction we highly recommend. We were able to have an amazing time looking at and holding turtles,  with turtles, looking at alligators and sharks, feeding birds, sliding down a fun water slide, and we even saw a variety of wild lizards!  This internationally renowned research and conservation center for sea turtles was a memorable part of our trip.  The reason you only see some of us for most of this experience and Zac just does a couple activities is because we were at the doctor for his eye most of the day.  This was the day after he was in an accident on the Carnival Magic Cruise Ship in the waterpark where the water pressure was too high and sprayed him full force directly in the eye. My kids went with their super nice grandparents, aunt, uncle and cousins so they could still participate in this excursion.  We are thankful they took our kids for the day for us!

Here is the recipe we used:
4 tablespoons of butter
4 tablespoons of flour
3 cups of milk
2 teaspoons of salt
A few shakes of pepper (just what you prefer for your tastes)
**We add more milk than some bechamel recipes call for in order to make it thinner for a pasta sauce**
We also use margarine instead of butter, so we used more of it that normal.  If you are using real butter, 3 tablespoons of butter/flour and 3 cups of milk will do.

CWgomBQzUyc.description:
So this is the biggest disaster Michael has ever caused.  My mom had just flown in and wanted to see the kids before they went to bed.  We were out, about to grab something at the grocery store, so we came back home to see Papa and Nanny first. We had just sat down on the couch to hear about my mom's trip when i asked where Michael was (it was awfully quiet).  A few moments later, I heard this sound but couldn't quite pinpoint the sound. I wondered if Michael was in his favorite place (sarcastic)...the bathroom.  I started realizing it sounded like water being poured or sprayed, so we ran to the bathroom.  Water was literally POURING from the toilet. Talk about a mess.  We don't even know how Michael plugged the toilet in order to get it to overflow like that, but we think one of the twins left a pair of shorts on the floor when he had gone to the bathroom and michael tried to flush them along with a bunch of toilet paper.  The toilet still isn't quite working right so we will be removing it and investigating further this weekend...
It's tricky because the other little kids in the house have trouble remembering to shut the bathroom door behind them, then Michael can get into the bathroom.  Toilet locks also aren't an option because when the twins have to use the bathroom, they usually wait till the last minute, so they have an accident if they have to wait.  So for now, we just have to be more diligent about keeping the bathroom door shut when Michael is not in his play area.

5YJCKT90km8.description:
Introducing our new car, the Nissan NV.  After MUCH research, we finally found a car that was big enough for us--and our two strollers, 5 kids car seats, 4 soccer chairs, soccer gear, diaper bags, spare clothes and all other kid related stuff that makes its way into a car-- but it's not a weird car!  Well, maybe some of you will think it's weird, but it's a great car so far! Many big cars (like the Mercedes Sprinter that we looked at) don't have all the features that this car has, such as the automatic seats, dual air, lots of cup holders, storage up front, seat warmers, charging ports in the back, pronged plug outlets, touch screen center panel, heated mirrors, towing, leather, etc, etc.  The NV is longer than some cars, but not that much wider, so we still fit in normal parking spaces, and our car fits in the garage--this was a huge thing for us.  Some of the other big cars were too tall to fit in the garage, but this one fits easily. This car also makes me feel very safe because it's big and heavy and taller than  many other cars. There's plenty of room so if a car were to hit us, there's some space between the kids and the sides of the car.  There are car seat hooks on every row, and plenty of space inside for some awesome roadtrips that we are now planning to take!

Hi-1buFC5lQ.description:
This video is for parents, by parents. For this video, we filmed our son over the period of almost a week, whenever he went on his own to use the Activity Garden, that we purchased.  Although I think a price point of $60-$70 would be a better value for this item, he really loves the Activity Garden.  He loves opening and shutting the door and crawling down the little blue slide.  I just wish there was a little more attention to detail paid when designing the product.  I think they should have made the round parts of the arch above the slide into spinners.  There's these cute stickers on the round part, and I have seen my son go up to them and try to spin them around, but they don't move.  Also, the telescope is cute, but not really something that would interest someone in the age group that would be playing in this.  The garden is so small that it is definitely meant for someone under the age of 2, but usually telescopes aren't cool till they are over 2 years old.  Perhaps a pretend flower that makes clicking noises would have been better to place there instead of the telescope.  A feature that I like that I forgot to mention in the video is that because you can reconfigure the garden, it does come apart and make for easy transportation and storage, unlike many other similar products. Buy it here: http://amzn.to/1MH7u06

9pCwfDIpH_I.description:
This is a video review done by the kids of their Step 2 Skyward Summit.  It has to be one of the coolest toys a kid could own.  We got this toy from our Great Grandpa.  The toy is meant for kids aged 4-8 (all 4 of our big kids are within that bracket), but we have had older and younger friends over to play and they have all enjoyed our Mountain.  Although it's only a few large pieces, it actually took a little more effort to put this together than we had anticipated.  It is very difficult to attach the rope ladder.  There is no give in the rope, so stretching it is not an option.  We ended up removing the bar along the bottom so we could push the plastic a bit to get the rope ladder to attach.  After the rope ladder is attached to the blue side pieces, you are supposed to use a couple washers and a long screw to attach the top of the net from the inside by the landing zone to the outside of the green and orange pieces.  Even when removing the washers, there just was no way we could get all of the screws in place.  We finally gave up after over an hour of trying and let the kids play on it without the rope ladder on one side.  The next day, we went to the hardware store and got a longer screw in order to finish the project.  One thing I noticed while researching this toy online was that in all of the images, it appears to be a square.  The base of the toy is in fact a rectangle.  The blue sides are longer than the orange and green ones.  Also, in the online images, I couldn't tell that there was the landing zone in the center of the toy.  It makes sense to have it there so they don't fall 7 feet down when they go through the hole in the top of the purple part.  It's kind of a trampoline-like material.  The kids LOVE this toy.  They play on it every single day.  Wanna see what we did with the huge box this came in???  Video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8WavWFB3IHI

Jh0pOf1IQjE.description:
I have always kind of wondered when the "right time" is to let your little girl get her ears pierced.  I decided I wanted her to be old enough to want to do it, rather than doing it as a baby.  When she was little, I would say that I would wait for her to ask, then make her complete a bunch of hard songs on the piano....well, I didn't realize when she was a baby that she was going to be so good at the piano at such a young age, so leveraging piano practice for ear piercing was out the door.  In fact, I have been asking her for the past few years if she wanted to do it and she always said no!  Finally, just before her first vocal showcase (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RuFAfGhgErE) her friend came over and had her ears pierced.  Again, I asked and thought it would be the perfect time to let her feel extra pretty and confident going into her first big performance.  After she thought about it all day, she came and told me she had decided all by herself that she wanted to get her ears pierced.  So, the day before her show, we got them done.  I think they look cute on her and she loves them!
*this video is graphic, it is not for children

8LXu9BhUaoo.description:
This is one of our oldest videos.  It's just life around here, and I'm glad we have this memory because life has sure changed now that everyone is a bit older!  While i was showering (before filming this clip), my twins dumped out over 10 pounds of popcorn on the kitchen floor.  They climbed over the baby gate and up 4 shelves in the pantry in order to get it down. My oldest (just turned 5 yrs old) got the popcorn popper down and the kids started popping popcorn.  Once i turned off the camera and started cleaning, they were grabbing handfuls of kernels and throwing them around the house as fast as they could.....let's just say they had a blast, but it's been over a month and I am still finding popcorn in my carpet.

fJ7qFXneLpk.description:
PART 2 of Twins Putting Themselves to Bed:  https://youtu.be/gEXPmgHmQ0Y
And so here's our story...this is our VERY first YouTube video.  I took this video for family who lives far away, so they could see how the family was growing and becoming pretty athletic at a young age.  We never taught them to do this.  One day i told the Zac & Chris, identical twin brothers, to go to bed and they did it!  They just ran to bed and hopped in!  I was shocked, and now they do it on a regular basis.  This is their favorite part of the day, when they get to parkour themselves into their beds together and see who makes it in first.  They are 1.5 yrs in this video.  The crib tents are to keep them safe if they wake up while we are sleeping, because they tend to silently climb out and try to go in places that could be dangerous for them, and they help to keep bugs out of the cribs, just in case.  They are also fire retardant, just in case anyone was worried :). and yes...we brush their teeth after they fall asleep--a fabulous recommendation by our dentist!   Thanks for watching!
